name: Dulaglutide
used_for: FDA-labeled (Trulicity) as an adjunct to diet and exercise for glycemic control in adults and children 10 and older with type 2 diabetes, and to reduce major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes who have established cardiovascular disease or multiple cardiovascular risk factors. It is not labeled for weight loss. The label carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumors.

entries.text: Adults: labeled starting dosage 0.75 mg subcutaneously once weekly; after 4 weeks it may be increased to 1.5 mg weekly, then in 1.5 mg steps after at least 4 weeks on the current dose, up to a labeled maximum of 4.5 mg once weekly.
entries.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes per the Trulicity label

entries.text: Children: labeled starting dosage 0.75 mg subcutaneously once weekly, which may be increased after at least 4 weeks to the labeled maximum of 1.5 mg once weekly.
entries.population: Patients aged 10 years and older with type 2 diabetes per the Trulicity label

administration_guidance.text: The Trulicity label states the drug is administered once weekly at any time of day with or without food, subcutaneously in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Trulicity label states a missed dose is given as soon as possible if at least 3 days (72 hours) remain until the next scheduled dose, and is skipped if less than 3 days remain, after which the regular weekly schedule resumes.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Trulicity label states the pen is stored in a refrigerator (2 to 8 C), may be kept at room temperature not above 30 C for a total of 14 days, is not frozen or used if frozen, and is protected from light, preferably in the original carton.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Trulicity label states the day of weekly administration can be changed if necessary, as long as the last dose was given 3 or more days before the new day. It also states that when used with insulin, the products are injected separately and never mixed, and may be given in the same body region but not adjacent to each other.
administration_guidance.label: research

side_effects.text: In the Trulicity label's placebo-controlled trials, nausea occurred in 12.4% (lower dose) and 21.1% (higher dose) vs 5.3% with placebo, vomiting 6.0 and 12.7% vs 2.3%, diarrhea 8.9 and 12.6% vs 6.7%, abdominal pain 6.5 and 9.4% vs 4.9%, and decreased appetite 4.9 and 8.6% vs 1.6%.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Trulicity label reports gastrointestinal adverse reactions in 32% and 41% of participants on the two doses vs 21% with placebo, with higher rates of discontinuation due to these reactions.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Trulicity label carries a boxed warning of thyroid C-cell tumors in rats, with unknown human relevance, and lists warnings for acute pancreatitis and acute gallbladder disease.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: WebMD patient reviews of Trulicity average 3.3 of 5; reviewers often cite better blood sugar, about a quarter mention weight loss or less appetite, and many report nausea, vomiting, other digestive problems or injection-site pain.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Trulicity (dulaglutide) injection (Eli Lilly), published August 2026.
research.finding: Lists approved uses for type 2 diabetes glycemic control (adults and patients 10 and older) and cardiovascular risk reduction; weekly dosing from 0.75 mg up to 4.5 mg in adults; boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors.

research.summary: REWIND: double-blind trial of dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly versus placebo in 9,901 adults with type 2 diabetes, median follow-up 5.4 years (Gerstein et al., Lancet).
research.finding: The composite of cardiovascular death, heart attack or stroke occurred in 12.0% with dulaglutide versus 13.4% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.88). All-cause death did not differ significantly. Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported by 47.4% versus 34.1%. Funded by Eli Lilly.

research.summary: AWARD-6: 26-week open-label non-inferiority trial of weekly dulaglutide versus daily liraglutide in 599 metformin-treated adults with type 2 diabetes (Dungan et al., Lancet).
research.finding: HbA1c fell 1.42% with dulaglutide and 1.36% with liraglutide; dulaglutide was non-inferior, with similar tolerability. Open-label and sponsor-funded.

research.summary: AWARD-PEDS: placebo-controlled trial of weekly dulaglutide 0.75 or 1.5 mg in 154 youths with type 2 diabetes, 26 weeks (Arslanian et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: HbA1c rose 0.6 points with placebo and fell 0.6 (0.75 mg) and 0.9 (1.5 mg) with dulaglutide; there was no BMI effect, and gastrointestinal events were more common with dulaglutide. Funded by Eli Lilly.

dose.summary: Labeled for adults at 0.75 mg once a week, raised in steps to a maximum of 4.5 mg. Children 10 and older start at 0.75 mg and can go up to 1.5 mg. No dose change is advised for kidney disease.

cycle_length.summary: It is used long term, with no planned cycles. Trials ran 26 weeks and, in the heart trial, a median of 5.4 years. No study of what happens after stopping was found. Some long-term patient reviewers report better results after the first adjustment period.

mechanism.summary: A long-acting version of the gut hormone GLP-1. It raises insulin when blood sugar is high and slows stomach emptying.

items.text: The Trulicity label states dulaglutide activates the GLP-1 receptor, a cell-surface receptor coupled to adenylyl cyclase in pancreatic beta cells.
items.label: research

items.text: The Trulicity label states dulaglutide delays gastric emptying in a dose-dependent way.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: In REWIND, 12.0% of people on dulaglutide had a heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death versus 13.4% on placebo over 5.4 years. In AWARD-6 it lowered HbA1c (a blood sugar measure) by 1.42 points. Patient reviewers mention blood sugar gains and some weight loss, which is not a labeled use.

side_effect_groups.title: Low blood sugar
side_effect_groups.summary: Low blood sugar is mainly a risk when combined with a sulfonylurea (20% to 21%) or mealtime insulin (69% to 77%).

items.text: The Trulicity label states hypoglycemia (glucose below 54 mg/dL) occurred in 20% and 21% of patients on 0.75 mg and 1.5 mg when co-administered with a sulfonylurea, and in 77% and 69% when co-administered with prandial insulin in a 52-week trial.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.summary: WebMD reviewers report nausea and vomiting (38%), often starting around the second day after the shot, and injection-site pain (11%).
